children: Raymond James's Michael Barth is scratching his head after Canadian Natural Resources agreed on the latest transaction in a string of deals over the last 18 months. Canadian Natural is buying smaller Advantage Energy for C$2.53 billion including debt, which Barth calculates works out to a not particularly expensive roughly C$30,000 per barrel a day based on the expected 2027 production the assets will bring. Still, given Advantage Energy's portfolio is largely dry gas, Barth questions whether this acquisition is a better use of cash than continued share buybacks. The analyst says ultimately the transaction in isolation isn't particularly material, so he retains a market perform call on Canadian Natural's shares. Canadian Natural Resources is down 2.4% at C$69.19. (robb.stewart@wsj.com)
